html:
The conversion of the kingdom of Armenia to Christianity, by tradition in 301, which made it the first state to adopt Christianity as its official religion. Some historians prefer a date around 314.

By Armenian tradition, King Tiridates III had persecuted Christians and kept Gregory the Illuminator in a pit for thirteen years. When the king fell ill, Gregory cured him, and the king and his court were baptised. Gregory became the first head of the Armenian Church, and the cathedral of Etchmiadzin was built.

This came over a decade before the Roman emperor Constantine made the faith legal in the Edict of Milan. Armenia, caught between Rome and Sasanian Persia, came to define itself by its church. Around 405 the monk Mesrop Mashtots created the Armenian alphabet to translate the Bible. Its neighbour Iberia, in Georgia, converted in the 330s.
